profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a public company founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, WA. Its website, in the context captured here, focuses on Power Automate, which the company describes as a tool for automating workflows and business processes across apps, systems, and websites using AI-powered, digital, and robotic process automation. The site quotes a customer saying that a data validation process previously requiring over 100 people can now be managed by just a few people using generative AI and Power Automate, and references a Gartner Magic Quadrant for Robotic Process Automation report dated 23 June 2025 listing Arthur Villa, Saikat Ray, Melanie Alexander, and Sachin Joshi as authors.

Microsoft's tracked AI product portfolio spans multiple categories. In automation and agents the site tracks Microsoft Power Automate AI, which includes Copilot integration, M365 data access, and DLP integration. Across chat and general use, Microsoft Copilot is embedded throughout M365. Cloud AI services include Azure OpenAI Service, which offers OpenAI models in Azure regions with enterprise content filtering and Entra ID integration, and Azure Machine Learning, an MLOps platform with AutoML and a model registry. Developer tools include AutoGen, a multi-agent conversation framework from Microsoft Research, Semantic Kernel, a model-agnostic orchestration SDK for .NET, Python, and Java, and Microsoft Agent Framework, described as the successor to both Semantic Kernel and AutoGen with native MCP and A2A support, expected in 2026. Additional products cover image generation via Microsoft Designer, meeting and knowledge tools in Microsoft Teams AI and SharePoint AI, and video editing through Microsoft Clipchamp AI.

On the legal and financial side, Microsoft reported revenue of $331,839,000,000 for the period ending 30 June 2026, filed as a 10-K under CIK 0000789019 and ticker MSFT. The held facts associate Microsoft with 60 legal matters in Washington state. Microsoft is also named as a defendant in The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and appears in related litigation, Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., in the same court.
